skyport.ponder.airport_station.text_1: The Airport Station defines one airport. Name it, then draw its layout on a map of the surrounding terrain.
skyport.ponder.airport_station.text_2: Draw the runway first - two points, gate end then far end. Everything else connects to it.
skyport.ponder.airport_station.text_3: Taxiway clicks are read in PAIRS. Each pair is one segment: a backbone from the runway, then a spur out to each gate.
skyport.ponder.airport_station.text_4: A Hold Line on the taxiway is where aircraft queue for the runway. Gates and Pads are where they park.
skyport.ponder.airport_station.text_5: The Holding Pattern is a loop flown in the air, at its own altitude. Arrivals circle here when the runway is busy.
skyport.ponder.airport_station.text_6: The Final Leg runs FROM the pattern TO the runway - draw it that way round. Aircraft descend along it to land.
skyport.ponder.airport_station.text_7: Hold this block to see the layout traced in the world, so you can build a runway where you drew one.
skyport.ponder.autopilot.text_1: The Autopilot flies one aircraft. Place it on the craft with the arrow on top pointing along the fuselage.
skyport.ponder.autopilot.text_2: That arrow is how it knows which way the nose faces - a craft is just a pile of blocks otherwise.
skyport.ponder.autopilot.text_3: Build a schedule of stops, like a train's. Each stop waits for a timer, a player, or cargo to be loaded or unloaded.
skyport.ponder.autopilot.text_4: Choose Plane, Heli or Blimp. Planes need a runway; the other two lift straight off a pad.
skyport.ponder.autopilot.text_5: Engage it from that screen, or feed the block a redstone signal.
skyport.ponder.autopilot.text_6: Cutting that signal disengages the autopilot, even mid-flight, and hands the craft back. It reads the level, not a pulse, so a lever left on still means "flying" after a reload.
skyport.ponder.atc.text_1: Air Traffic Control shows every airport and every aircraft under autopilot on one live map.
skyport.ponder.atc.text_2: Drag to pan, scroll to zoom. The strip on the right lists each aircraft and what it is doing right now.
skyport.ponder.atc.text_3: Point a Create Display Link at this block, or at a station, to put the same traffic on a departures board.
skyport.ponder.atc.text_4: Opening it also wakes aircraft parked at airports nobody is visiting, so their schedules pick up again.
